mainTopic: End of פרק כל הנשבעין (גלגול שבועה, שביעית cancelling an oath) and the opening משנה of פרק שבועת הפקדון on the four שומרים and false oaths about a deposit
overview: This amud first finishes an argument about גלגול שבועה, the rule that a person who must swear can be made to include other claims in that oath. Both opinions agree that a hired worker's oath (שבועת שכיר) is not rolled over. They differ about everyone else: does the בית דין bring up the extra oath on its own, or only when the other side asks? The גמרא then learns from the words 'וזה דבר השמטה' that שביעית cancels even an oath about a loan. The chapter כל הנשבעין closes with a הדרן. A new משנה opens by listing the four kinds of guardians: שומר חנם, שואל, נושא שכר, and שוכר. It explains when each one swears and goes free and when each one must pay. It then brings cases where a guardian swears falsely about what happened to the ox, showing when he is פטור and when he pays קרן, כפל, or קרן, חומש and an אשם. It also covers a plain thief, who pays כפל or ארבעה וחמשה, or only the קרן if he admits first. The amud ends just as the borrower's case begins; his answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Every oath can be rolled over except a hired worker's
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion, which the גמרא brought just before this, says that גלגול שבועה works on every oath, even a rabbinic one. The one exception is the oath of a שכיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For every oath we roll on extra oaths, except a hired worker's oath, which we do not roll over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an opinion it started just before: גלגול applies to every oath except the oath of a שכיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גלגול שבועה means that once a person has to swear, the other side can add more claims into that same oath. This opinion says it works even on oaths that are only rabbinic. A שכיר's oath is different because the חכמים set it up to calm the employer's mind, so it is not rolled over at all.

keyTerms.meaning: We 'roll on' extra oaths: someone who already has to swear must also swear about other claims
A hired worker
Except for

phrases.english: For all oaths we roll over additional oaths,
except for a hired worker – for whom we do not roll over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of גלגול on rabbinic oaths
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גלגול applies to all oaths, even rabbinic ones, but not to the oath of a שכיר.

steps.title: רב חסדא: we are lenient only with a hired worker
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא puts it the other way around. For everyone we are not lenient, so we do roll over, except a שכיר, for whom we are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says: For everyone we are not lenient, except a hired worker, for whom we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives his own version of the rule. It sounds almost the same as the first opinion, but he uses the word 'lenient' instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that a שכיר's oath is not rolled over. The wording differs about everyone else: the first says 'we roll over', and רב חסדא says 'we are not lenient', which sounds stricter. The next steps ask what practical difference that makes.

keyTerms.meaning: We are lenient

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: לַכֹּל אֵין מְקִילִּין,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda says: For everyone we are not lenient,
except for a hired worker – with whom we are lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: לַכֹּל אֵין מְקִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the rule about the שכיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We are strict and roll over oaths for everyone, but we are lenient with a שכיר.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The two opinions sound alike, so the גמרא asks where they actually differ in practice. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whenever two rulings seem to say the same thing, the גמרא looks for a real case where they would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two opinions just stated
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where the two opinions would rule differently

steps.title: The difference: does the court raise it on its own?
steps.stepSummary: They differ about whether the בית דין itself starts the גלגול without being asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding opening for him, meaning whether the court raises the rolling over by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ about whether the court itself starts (לפתוח לו) the extra oath when the other side has not asked for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a שכיר's oath is not rolled over. They differ about everyone else. According to רש״י, the first opinion says 'we roll over', so the בית דין brings up the גלגול on its own, even if nobody asks. רב חסדא only says 'we are not lenient', so if the other side asks, we roll over. If nobody asks, the בית דין does not raise it by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
To open for him: the court raises the matter by itself

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree that a שכיר's oath is not rolled over. They argue about everyone else: does the בית דין raise the גלגול on its own, or only if the other side asks?

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding opening for him.
phrases.notes: 'Opening for him' means the court brings up the extra oath by itself, without the other side asking.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ about whether, for oaths other than a שכיר's, the court starts the גלגול on its own initiative (רב חסדא) or only when the other side asks (first opinion).

steps.title: Where do we learn that שביעית cancels an oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that שביעית cancels an oath about a loan and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and the Sabbatical Year cancels, etc. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה, that שביעית cancels the oath, and asks for its source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that שביעית cancels the loan itself. The new point here is that it also cancels the oath that would have been taken about that loan, so the גמרא wants a פסוק for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, which cancels loans
Releases or cancels
From where are these words learned?

phrases.english: And the Sabbatical Year cancels, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: שביעית cancels the oath about a loan, just as it cancels the loan.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְּׁבִיעִית מְשַׁמֶּטֶת כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that שביעית cancels an oath about a debt

steps.title: 'דבר השמטה' — even speech is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב learns it from the words 'וזה דבר השמטה'. The word דבר can also mean speech, so שביעית cancels even an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: The verse says 'And this is the matter of the release', which teaches that it releases even speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק, reading the word 'דבר' as 'speech' to include an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually 'דבר' here simply means 'matter'. Because it can also mean 'something spoken', רב reads it as teaching that שביעית cancels even what is spoken, meaning the oath connected to the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Matter, and also speech
Speech: here, the oath

steps.whatToRemember: Since שביעית cancels the loan, it also cancels any oath about that loan, learned from 'דבר השמטה'.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said,
for the verse states: “And this is the matter of the release” –
and it releases even speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וזה דבר השמטה': דבר also means speech, so שביעית cancels even the oath.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל הנשבעין
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the chapter כל הנשבעין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'All Who Take an Oath'.
steps.whatsHappening: This marks the end of the seventh chapter of שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a closing line that shows love for the chapter just finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you

phrases.english: We will return to you, “All who take an oath”

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כל הנשבעין is complete.

steps.title: The four types of guardians
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists four kinds of שומרים: an unpaid guardian, a borrower, a paid guardian, and a renter.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four guardians: an unpaid guardian, a borrower, a paid guardian, and a renter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. The משנה lists the four types of guardians, which sets up the rules that come next about when each one swears or pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each guardian is defined by two things: whether he is paid, and whether he gets to use the item. A שומר חנם gets nothing. A שואל uses the item for free. A נושא שכר is paid to watch it. A שוכר pays to use it. These differences decide how much responsibility each one has.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A guardian who is not paid
A borrower
A paid guardian
A renter

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up שכיר (hired worker, from the end of the last chapter) with שוכר (a renter who pays to use an item). They come from the same root but are different people.
steps.whyThisMatters: These four categories are the base for all the laws of guardians across ש״ס, especially in בבא מציעא.

phrases.english: MISHNA: There are four guardians:
an unpaid guardian and the borrower,
a paid guardian and the renter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four kinds of guardians: שומר חנם, שואל, נושא שכר, and שוכר.

steps.title: The unpaid guardian swears, the borrower always pays
steps.stepSummary: A שומר חנם can always swear and go free. A שואל must pay no matter what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: An unpaid guardian swears about everything, and the borrower pays for everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rule for the two most extreme שומרים from the list in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם gets nothing for his trouble, so he carries the least responsibility. Whatever happened to the animal, he swears he was not careless and goes free. A שואל gets all the benefit, so he carries the most responsibility and pays even for a true accident.

keyTerms.meaning: Swears about everything: he takes an oath in any case and goes free
Pays for everything, even an unavoidable accident
An accident outside a person's control

phrases.english: An unpaid guardian swears about everything,
and the borrower pays for everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rules for the guardians listed in Step 8, starting with the two extremes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שומר חנם: an oath frees him in every case. שואל: pays in every case.

steps.title: The paid guardian and the renter: swear on accidents, pay on loss and theft
steps.stepSummary: A נושא שכר and a שוכר swear and go free when the animal broke, was captured, or died. They must pay when it was lost or stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A paid guardian and a renter swear about an animal that was injured, captured, or died, and they pay for one that was lost or stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the middle level of responsibility, which belongs to the two remaining שומרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two get some benefit, so they carry more responsibility than a שומר חנם and less than a שואל. Breaking, capture, and death are true accidents, so they swear and go free. Loss and theft could have been stopped by watching more carefully, so they pay for those.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was injured or broken
An animal that was captured, for example by raiders
An animal that died
Something lost
Something stolen

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. A שומר חנם swears on everything. A שואל pays on everything. A נושא שכר and a שוכר swear on accidents (broken, captured, dead) and pay for loss and theft.

phrases.english: A paid guardian and the renter:
they swear about the injured animal
and about the captured one and about the dead one,
and they pay for the lost one and the stolen one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר וְהַשּׂוֹכֵר נִשְׁבָּעִין עַל הַשְּׁבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of rules by covering the two middle-level guardians.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נושא שכר and שוכר swear on broken, captured, or dead animals and pay for lost or stolen ones.

steps.title: An unpaid guardian swears to the wrong mishap and is still exempt
steps.stepSummary: A שומר חנם gives a false reason for what happened to the ox and swears to it. He is still פטור, because he would have been free whatever the true reason was.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner asks an unpaid guardian, "Where is my ox?" and he answers "It died" when really it was injured, captured, stolen, or lost, or he names any other one of these five mishaps when the truth was a different one, and the owner says "I make you swear" and he answers "Amen," he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a case where a שומר חנם lies under oath about how the ox was lost and rules that he is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם goes free in all five cases: dead, broken, captured, stolen, or lost. So swapping one true story for another false one does not save him any money he would otherwise owe. Because his lie took nothing from the owner, he does not have to bring the קרבן of a false oath about a deposit.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is my ox? (the owner's demand)
I make you swear: the owner puts the guardian under oath
Saying Amen to an oath counts as taking the oath yourself
Exempt
The oath about a deposit. Swearing falsely to keep someone's money brings a קרבן and an extra fifth

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean lying under oath is allowed. It means he does not have to bring the קרבן or pay the extra fifth for a false oath about a deposit, because his lie did not get him out of paying anything.

phrases.english: The owner said to an unpaid guardian: "Where is my ox?"
He said to him: "It died"

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה אוֹ נִגְנַב אוֹ אָבַד;
phrases.english: but really it was injured, or captured, or stolen, or lost;
or he said "It was injured," but really it died

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה אוֹ נִגְנַב אוֹ אָבַד.
phrases.english: or was captured, or stolen, or lost.
Or he said "It was captured," but really it died

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ נִשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִגְנַב אוֹ אָבַד;
phrases.english: or was injured, or stolen, or lost;
or he said "It was stolen," but really it died

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ נִשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה אוֹ אָבַד;
phrases.english: or was injured, or captured, or lost;
or he said "It was lost," but really it died

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ נִשְׁבַּר אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה אוֹ נִגְנַב;
phrases.english: or was injured, or captured, or stolen;
and the owner said "I make you swear," and he said "Amen"
he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Exempt from the קרבן for a false oath. Whatever really happened, an unpaid guardian wouldn't have had to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 9's rule that a שומר חנם is free in every case to decide what happens when he swears falsely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a שומר חנם falsely swears to one mishap when the truth was another, he is פטור from the קרבן of a false oath about a deposit.

steps.title: An unpaid guardian who denies knowing anything is also exempt
steps.stepSummary: A שומר חנם claims he has no idea what the owner is talking about, when really the ox suffered one of the five mishaps. He swears falsely and is still פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner asks, "Where is my ox?" and the guardian says, "I don't know what you are talking about," when really it died, was injured, captured, stolen, or lost, and the owner says "I make you swear" and he answers "Amen," he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes one step further. Even when the שומר חנם denies the whole deposit under oath, he is still פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This lie sounds worse, because he denies ever receiving the ox. But in truth the ox suffered one of the five mishaps, and a שומר חנם would have been free in all of them. So once again his false oath did not save him any money.

keyTerms.meaning: I don't know what you are talking about: a full denial of the deposit
Talking or saying
Denial of a claim

steps.whatToRemember: A שומר חנם's false oath leads to the קרבן only if the lie actually got him out of paying. When the true story would have freed him anyway, he is פטור, even if he denied the whole deposit.

phrases.english: "Where is my ox?" He said to him:
"I don't know what you are talking about"
but really it died, or was injured,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ נִשְׁבָּה אוֹ נִגְנַב אוֹ אָבַד;
phrases.english: or was captured, or stolen, or lost;
and the owner said "I make you swear," and he said "Amen"
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָן שׁוֹרִי אָמַר לוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה אַתָּה סָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends Step 11 from naming the wrong mishap to denying the deposit completely, with the same result of פטור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a full false denial under oath leaves a שומר חנם פטור, when the true mishap would have freed him anyway.

steps.title: The guardian who said 'lost' but really ate the ox
steps.stepSummary: A שומר חנם falsely swears the ox was lost. Witnesses show he ate it, so he pays the קרן. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש, and brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner asks, 'Where is my ox?' The guardian says, 'It got lost.' The owner says, 'I make you swear,' and he answers 'Amen.' Then witnesses testify that he ate it. He pays the value of the ox. If he admitted it on his own, he pays the value, plus an extra fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now shows a case where the שומר חנם's false oath does make him liable, because he himself ate the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 11 and 12 the lie did not matter, since he would have been פטור anyway. Here the truth is that he ate the ox, so he really owes for it. Because he claimed 'lost' and not 'stolen', he pays only the קרן, with no double payment. If he confesses on his own after swearing, he pays קרן plus חומש and brings an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear: the owner puts him under oath
The principal, meaning the actual value of the ox
He admitted on his own, without witnesses
An extra fifth added on top of the value
A guilt-offering brought for a false oath

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'witnesses caught him' is worse than 'admitted' in every way. With witnesses he pays only the קרן. Admitting on his own after a false oath is what brings in the חומש and the אשם.

phrases.english: "Where is my ox?" He said to him: "It got lost";
"I make you swear," and he said "Amen";
and witnesses testify about him that he ate it,
he pays the principal.
If he admitted on his own,
he pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with steps 11 and 12: there the lie made no difference. Here the truth makes him liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר חנם who falsely swore 'lost' but ate the ox pays only the קרן if witnesses show it. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and an אשם.

steps.title: The guardian who said 'stolen' but stole it himself
steps.stepSummary: A שומר חנם falsely swears the ox was stolen, and witnesses show he stole it himself. He pays תשלומי כפל. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner asks, 'Where is my ox?' The guardian says, 'It was stolen.' The owner says, 'I make you swear,' and he answers 'Amen.' Then witnesses testify that he himself stole it. He pays double. If he admitted it on his own, he pays the value, plus an extra fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the matching case where the false claim was 'stolen' instead of 'lost'. This time the penalty is a double payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from step 13 is the claim: 'stolen' instead of 'lost'. Falsely claiming it was stolen, when he took it himself, makes him pay כפל, just like a thief. Admitting on his own leads to the same result as before: קרן, חומש and אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stolen (the guardian's false claim)
Double payment, the penalty a thief pays

steps.whyThisMatters: Steps 13 and 14 show that the exact words of the false claim ('lost' or 'stolen') decide whether he pays only the value or double.

phrases.english: "Where is my ox?" And he said to him: "It was stolen";
"I make you swear," and he said "Amen";
and witnesses testify about him that he stole it,
phrases.notes: The thief here is the guardian himself, the one who claimed someone else stole it.

phrases.english: he pays double payment.
If he admitted on his own,
he pays the principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 13, but the claim is 'stolen', which raises the penalty to כפל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר חנם who falsely swore 'stolen' but stole it himself pays כפל if witnesses show it. If he admits on his own, he pays קרן, חומש and an אשם.

steps.title: A stranger accused of stealing the ox
steps.stepSummary: Someone in the market denies stealing the ox, and witnesses show he did. He pays כפל. If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner says to someone in the market, 'Where is my ox that you stole?' He answers, 'I didn't steal it.' Witnesses testify that he did. He pays double. If he slaughtered it or sold it, he pays four or five times its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches from a guardian to an ordinary person accused of theft. It gives the regular thief's penalties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person is not a שומר, so he never had the ox legally. He is just a thief. Witnesses make him pay כפל. If he also slaughtered or sold the animal, the penalty rises to four or five times its value.

keyTerms.meaning: In the marketplace, meaning a stranger who is not a guardian
Slaughtered or sold the stolen animal
Fourfold or fivefold payment for a stolen animal that was slaughtered or sold

phrases.english: If he said to someone in the marketplace:
"Where is my ox that you stole?"
He says: "I did not steal it,"
and witnesses testify about him that he stole it,
he pays double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְאֶחָד בַּשּׁוּק: הֵיכָן שׁוֹרִי שֶׁגָּנַבְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a guardian who stole to a plain thief.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief caught by witnesses pays כפל. If he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Admitting before the witnesses arrive
steps.stepSummary: The thief sees witnesses coming and admits to the theft only, saying he did not slaughter or sell it. He pays only the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he saw witnesses on their way and said, 'I stole it, but I didn't slaughter it or sell it,' he pays only the value of the ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows how the thief's own admission, made before the witnesses testify, changes his payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Double payment and four-or-five payment are fines. Once he admits the theft himself, he no longer pays the fine for it. So he pays only the קרן, even though he could tell witnesses were about to testify against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Coming closer, about to arrive
He pays only the principal

steps.whatToRemember: With a plain thief: if witnesses prove it, he pays כפל (or ארבעה וחמשה). If he admits first, he pays only the קרן, even when he sees the witnesses coming.

phrases.english: If he saw witnesses that were on their way,
and he said: "I stole it,
but I did not slaughter it and did not sell it,"
he pays only the principal.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief who admits before the witnesses testify pays only the קרן.

steps.title: Starting the borrower's case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new case: the owner asks a שואל where his ox is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner said to a borrower, 'Where is my ox?' and the borrower said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה opens the borrower's case, and his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 9 we know a שואל pays no matter what happens to the animal. The משנה is now setting up the same 'Where is my ox?' pattern for him. The ruling is still to come.
